newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest prices ease, Southwest moves higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest prices ease, Southwest moves higher.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices eased in the northwestern U.S. for Friday and Monday delivery on forecasts of seasonal weather returning to the region, while prices rose in the Southwest, traders said.
Trade was scarce Wednesday with many traders leaving early for the Thanksgiving Day holiday Thursday and planning to take a day off on Friday.
Bonneville Power Administration held its prices relatively steady for Sunday and Monday delivery at levels that some traders said were too high to be worth considering.

BPA offered up to 300 megawatts of peak power for Monday at $32.00 in the Northwest and $32.75 at the California Oregon Border (COB). Sunday peak power, with a 500 MW limit, was offered at $30.00 in the Northwest and $30.75 at COB.
Basin Electric Power Cooperative said it expects a 550 megawatt coal fired unit 3 at its Laramie River Station in Wyoming to be taken off line Wednesday for maintenance and restart output Sunday.
Southern California Edison's 1,070 megawatt San Onofre nuclear power unit 2 was expected to come off line early Sunday morning for 70 days of scheduled refueling and maintenance.

Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 in central California was scheduled to resume operation by Friday after tripping off line November 22 when a fire hit an auxiliary power grounding transformer.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Friday was down slightly at $29.00-31.00 from next-day power discussion at $31.75-$32.25 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Firm, off-peak COB power for the weekend and Monday was also said to be talked at $29.00-31.00, with firm, off-peak assessed at $17.00-$18.00, the sources said.
December COB deliveries were assessed down slightly at $28.00-29.00 from $28.25-$29.25 on Tuesday, while January COB held steady at $25.25-$25.50, the sources said.
First-quarter 1997 COB was valued higher at $21.50-22.00 from $21.25-$21.40 on Tuesday.

Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was notionally discussed lower at $25.00-27.00 for Friday but up to $28.00-30.00 for Monday, from discussion on Tuesday at $30.75-$31.25, the sources said.
Next-day firm, off-peak Mid-C values were notionally talked steady to lower at $14.00-17.00 from a notional assessment at $18.50-$19.50 on Tuesday.
December Mid-C was quoted higher at $27.50-28.50 from $27.00-$28.00 on Tuesday.
In the Southwest, next-day power deliveries were said to be talked higher through to Monday after a sell-off Tuesday afternoon.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) power was talked at $28.00-29.00 for Friday from talk at $20.00-$21.00 on Tuesday.
PV peak power for Monday delivery was assessed at $25.00-27.00, the sources said.
Firm, off-peak PV electricity was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-$14.00.
December PV power was assessed higher at $28.00-29.00 from $27.00-$28.00, while January PV was valued at $25.50-26.50 from $24.00-$25.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
First-quarter 1997 PV deliveries were discussed higher at $22.00-22.75 from $21.50-$21.90 on Tuesday.
Four Corners firm, peak power for Friday delivery was notionally assessed higher at $23.00-25.00 while Monday was pegged at $25.50-26.50 from discussion at $21.00-$23.00 on Tuesday.
Four Corners firm, off-peak power for Friday was notationally assessed steady at $14.00-$17.00.
--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627
